title: Coach
summary: The board explains each King Down rule at the moment it matters, with quiet marks and one line under the board. The help fades by level: full at Beginner, quiet at Club.
problem: Every King Down player is new: six new pieces, twelve powers, shots over pieces. A chess player loses to rules that are hard to see, and today the help lives in menus and lessons, far from the move.
idea: Teach on the board, inside a real game. A badge on a new piece, hold to read, peek with ghosts and danger rings, a refusal that names its rule, the ways out of check, and Retry from the move that lost the game.

borrows.what: Show every threat before you commit, so a loss is your own choice. Peek and the danger rings come from its telegraphs.
No hidden rule: a refusal shows its cause on the board, with one plain line.
Keyword help at the point of need: the Guard's shield and one line, only when you touch it.
A second try: after a loss, Retry from the move that turned the game, not from the start.
Teach at first meeting, in play, then step back. The help fades by level and by use.

options.name: Full help (Beginner, Casual)
options.summary: A badge on a new piece, peek with ghosts and danger rings, refusal lines, the ways out of check as chips, Retry after a loss.

options.name: Quiet help (Club, Strong)
options.summary: Only hold to read, refusals and cause lines. Check shows its cause line and one sentence. No chips, no badge, no peek, no Retry.

recommendation: Use Coach for a player's first ten games, then let it fade into Quiet help. Keep one Board help switch so a player can choose: it changes the marks, never the computer's level. Peek shows the rules only, never the computer's plan.
notes: Look at refusal and check: the rule names itself at the cause, and the ways out are real engine moves.
Look at retry, then retried: Retry goes back to move 17, selects your beast and shows the shot that took it.
The shared states come from P1, the scripted line and P2. Open ?state=check&frame=phone to show one state in one layout.
Retry uses a real lost game from P1: the Beginner computer plays White, the Club computer plays Black. The turn is your last move before they took a piece that is not a pawn.

Play it: hold a piece to read it. Select a piece, then rest the mouse on a marked square or hold it with a finger to peek. A lift after a peek plays nothing; a tap plays. Tap the pawn on d3, then the Guard. Menu holds the Board help switch.
Limits: the Archer's empty shot squares do not show (the kit gives legal moves only). Peek looks one reply ahead, not deeper. Sounds are the kit's tones.
The goals line and Second look are not in this demo.
